public_rationale: The court found actual harms from reliance on ChatGPT-generated fake authorities, with conduct continuing after Marcus's post. This satisfies the broad prediction that LLM use would cause harm. Human misconduct also contributed. [Judicial opinion](https://caselaw.findlaw.com/court/us-dis-crt-sd-new-yor/2335142.html).
limitations: This establishes that harm occurred, not its prevalence or the forecast's probability calibration.
The court attributed responsibility to the lawyers; the finding does not make LLM use the sole cause.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Large language models are almost certain to cause harm.

statement.excerpt: But they are almost certain to cause harm as well, and we need to prepare for that, too.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading predicts actual harm from LLM outputs or misuse, without specifying its severity, prevalence, or deadline.
At least one verified instance of harm after publication can establish the predicted outcome. It cannot establish the numerical probability implied by 'almost certain'.
Human misuse may contribute to the harm; the model need not be its sole cause.
criteria.support_condition: A documented event after 2023-03-10 establishes actual harm caused or materially enabled by an LLM output or misuse.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A finite period without documented harm cannot disprove this forecast without a deadline. Failure of a particular alleged example would not contradict the general claim.
